kind: declaration — stated before the 27 receded endpoints are fitted and before any of their rows is read
tier: WebGPU. The CSS tier derives from the same documents and is recorded beside; it gates nothing here, exactly as in W27c G1b.
rules: W29 Decision Log 6 (d), ruled by the user 2026-09-19: the bound is declared before the read 'in the form and at the values W28's §5.134 §6 bound.json used for the 26.5 recede'. Contracts X1, X3, X5, X7.
$comment: This is `results/2026-09-11-w27c-g1b/bound.json` — the bound W27c G1b declared
for the 26.5 recede and W28 G2 scored 6 of 6 against — carried to the macOS 27
bed. Its three clauses, its metrics, its arithmetic and every one of its
eighteen thresholds are that file's, unchanged and not re-derived. What this
file decides is only what it HAS to decide: which 27 profile each 26.5
profile's thresholds attach to, and which cells are the checking set on a bed
whose splits are not W27c's checking-bed groups.
Both decisions are made here rather than after the read, and both are made by
a rule rather than by naming cells, so that neither can be chosen to be
passable.
Nothing in this file adopts a floor. Acceptance clause 4 of this wave rules a
27 regression floor out on every profile — the 27 bed sits at the seven-run
probe bar and not the seventeen-run freeze bar a floor needs (claims §5.150
Part B §4) — and the inactive pose is outside the adopted gate entirely on
both beds (claims §5.148; the gate drops the pose on every set). So a miss
here changes no CI gate and is a finding put to the user, which is the shape
Decision Log 4 (a) gave a miss and Decision Log 6 (d) repeats for this one.
The two 27 receded documents this child fits, posed through
`compare --receded-profile` over the 27 ACTIVE documents of the same read.
Their hashes are recorded in `sealed-documents.txt` BEFORE the canonical read
and the read refuses to run at any other bytes, exactly as G3's
`canonical-read.sh` refuses at any other active document.
The active material does not move in this child except for the outer shadow's
constants, which are Decision Log 6 (a)'s and are fitted and sealed in the
same wave. That is a deviation from W28 contract X10's 'the active material
does not move' as it stood for that wave, and it is named rather than
silently taken: the recede is read over the 27 active material as it will
SHIP, so reading it over a shadow this wave has already found to be wrong
would measure a pose against a body nobody intends to keep. The field diff of
the active documents is committed evidence (`document-diff.txt`) and it shows
the shadow block and nothing else.
W27c G1b scored group D of `checking-bed.json` and nothing else, on one rule:
a cell the fit was selected on, or a cell whose answer is already on the
record, may not decide whether the bound holds. W28's contract X11 states the
same rule as 'the checking set is never a selection cell'.
The 27 bed has no checking-bed groups — it is the declared bed, split
calibration / validation / holdout in `apps/reference-apple/scenes.json` — so
the rule is carried across by the split that already exists, which is the
translation with the fewest free choices in it:
the checking set is every INACTIVE cell of the VALIDATION and HOLDOUT sets,
on every 27 profile that declares one.
The inactive CALIBRATION rows are what the fit is selected on, so they are
group A/B/C's role here and are excluded by the same argument that excluded
those: 17 ids on the light standard profiles, 10 on the dark pair, 5 and 6 on
the two accessibility profiles. They are READ and PUBLISHED under clause 4,
as W27c's supplying cells were — outside the pass/fail arithmetic, not
outside the record.
The `recorded` and `probe` sets are excluded for the reason they are excluded
everywhere in this repository: `probe` is gated by nothing (W25 Decision Log
3 (e)) and `recorded` is not a fidelity set.
Counted from the manifest at declaration time, before any fit: 48 checking
cells across the six profiles — 16 on each light standard profile, 5 on each
dark standard profile, 3 on the coupled increased-contrast profile and 3 on
reduced transparency.
scope.scored: every inactive cell of the validation and holdout sets, on every 27 profile that declares one
scope.readAndPublishedButNotScored: the inactive calibration rows (the fit's selection cells), and the recorded and probe sets

$comment: The composite components. `bodyDeltaE` is a statistic over the DECLARED BOX
eroded 6 CSS px, and `toolbar-group` (three capsules with gaps) and
`glass-over-glass` (a pane on a pane) have no single declared box — the
reader returns null rather than inventing a rectangle, which is the same
absence `cli/native-delta-readers.ts` reports for them. Clause 1 is
full-canvas and scores them; clauses 2 and 3 cannot and say so.
Declared here rather than discovered at scoring time, with the count, so
that a scorer that silently dropped a cell would fail this file instead of
quietly narrowing the bound.

metrics.fullCanvasDeltaE: whole-image mean per-pixel OKLab distance — the canonical `oklabDeltaEMean` of the perceptual axis, read straight off the canonical `results/matrix.json` row, which is the same quantity `adopted-thresholds.test.ts` gates and the same one W27c G1b named
metrics.bodyDeltaE: the same distance over the declared box eroded 6 CSS px (`ERODE_CSS_PX`, `declaredBox` — W21's body, which W23 and W24 both read against), computed by this gate's `score-bound.ts` from the committed native fixture and the canonical web capture, because the matrix carries no eroded-body ΔE row and adding one would be a schema change this child has no reason to make

clauses.name: the ceiling — per cell, full-canvas
clauses.rule: Every cell of the checking set reads `oklabDeltaEMean` at or below its profile's threshold below.
reason: Exactly W27c G1b clause 1's six numbers, attached to the 27 profile each
26.5 profile's fixtures are the counterpart of (`counterpartKey` in
`cli/native-delta-metrics.ts`: the OS token moves and the slider token
drops, and the coupled contrast key is the one that names the 26.5
increased-contrast bed like for like — Decision Log 4 (b), claims §5.152).
They were, and still are, the bound the ACTIVE material is held to on the
same tier, the same profile and the same metric — the 27 tables of
`adopted-thresholds.test.ts` are ALIASES of the 26.5 ones by Decision Logs
4 (a) and 5, so 'the active bed's adopted ceiling' is the same number on
both beds and this clause does not have to choose between them. The inactive
pose ships into the same product through the same root, so it may not be
held to a weaker one.

clauses.name: the discriminating clause — per profile, interior
clauses.rule: The checking set's equal-cell mean `bodyDeltaE` for each profile is at or below the threshold below, over the cells that have a declared box.
reason: W27c G1b clause 2's six numbers, unchanged and at the same profile mapping.
Decision Log 6 (d) says 'at the values W28's §5.134 §6 bound.json used',
and these are them: each is the 26.5 frozen endpoint's own VALIDATION mean
body ΔE from the G1 read, rounded up to two significant figures.
Deriving 27 thresholds from a 27 reading instead was available and is
refused, because there is no 27 reading that could supply them which this
child has not also fitted against — the 26.5 numbers came from a frozen
experiment that predated the bound, and nothing on the 27 bed has that
property. A threshold computed from this child's own fit would be a bound
the fit could not fail.
What carrying them across DOES assume, stated because it is the assumption
a reader should test: that a 27 recede fitted as well as the 26.5 recede was
fitted should land in the same place on the same metric. The 27 material is
not the 26.5 material — §5.151 measured it moving on every cell — so this is
a bound on the QUALITY OF THE FIT and not on the material, and that is why
it is the right one to carry. A miss says this child fitted the 27 endpoints
less well than W28 fitted the 26.5 ones, or that the 27 recede has a
structure the existing operators cannot hold; the read has to say which.

clauses.name: the per-cell floor on a named residual
clauses.rule: No cell of the checking set with a declared box exceeds twice its profile's clause-2 threshold. A cell that does is named in the ledger, and no inactive floor may be adopted for the regime that cell identifies — which on this bed is every regime, since clause 4 of this wave adopts no 27 floor at all.
reason: W27c G1b clause 3, unchanged, including the multiple. A mean over a large
bed absorbs one bad cell, and every residual either bed has named is
concentrated in one or two cells; 2× is the smallest multiple that admitted
every validation cell of the frozen 26.5 read with margin while still
catching that bed's own known failures.

clauses.name: what is reported whether or not it gates
rule: The read publishes, per checking cell AND per supplying cell: both metrics, the resolved group state, the resolved pose readback, the candidate receded document the capture was posed with and its hash (which is in the cell's `capturePath`), the fixture set, the eroded-body level and standard deviation on both sides beside the distances, and the shadow axis.

The per-profile comparison is stated on `bodyDeltaE`. The full-canvas ratio between the checking set and the calibration set is NOT a gate quantity and is reported only with the two sets' footprint composition beside it — W27c G1b clause 4's rule, kept because the error it was written against (a ratio quoted across sets whose mean footprint differs 3.08×–3.68×) is available on this bed too.

clauses.name: what stops or refuses the read
rule: REFUSED, cell by cell, by the instruments that already do it: a capture whose reported canvas, requested scale or devicePixelRatio disagrees with the declaration (`captureIntegrityRefusal`); a capture whose resolved colour scheme is not the profile's, or which is filed under an inactive id without either an inactive root or a candidate receded document (`capturePoseRefusal`); a fallback adapter; a non-empty `problems`.

STOPPED if `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PROFILE` moves, if any of the 34 renderer goldens moves, or if either 26.5 profile document's resolved fingerprint moves (X1). The 27 receded documents are applied as a patch over the 27 active documents; the 26.5 bed must be byte-identical throughout, and `results/2026-09-16-w29-freeze/freeze.py verify` is run at this gate's opening and close.
SPENT once read: the holdout is read once at the sealed configuration and nothing is re-fitted after it (X5). A failed partial read is spent and is not silently retried as fresh.

whatHoldingMeans.holds: clauses 1, 2 and 3 hold JOINTLY on every profile the checking set covers. A profile that passes clause 2's mean and fails clause 3 on one cell has not held the bound — W27c G1b's own rule, and the one that made the 26.5 spent holdout fail four of six profiles where clause 2 alone would have failed two.
whatHoldingMeans.ifItMisses: nothing is re-fitted, no threshold is widened and no floor is adopted. The miss is recorded per profile per clause with the cell that carries it, and it is drafted for the user as a Decision Log entry in the shape Decision Log 4 (a) gave a dark ΔE miss: a floor decision for the user, recorded, not a bound loosened after the fact and not a fit failure.
whatHoldingMeans.whatItDoesNotDecide: whether the 27 receded endpoints are SELECTED by the runtime. That is W29 G4's by Decision Log 2, and it stays G4's whether this bound holds or misses: these documents are calibration profile documents posed through `compare --receded-profile`, and `packages/platform-web/src/receded-profile.ts` still ships the 26.5 endpoints.
